text:
Explicit structural revision of this unexecuted artifact. Preserve all accepted requirements and exact public outputs: filePath:string, products:array(maxItems:10) of nonnull objects {name:string?,description:string?,price:string?,error:string?}, browserClosed:boolean, success:boolean. Preserve input query, the exact writer destination, actual search and individual visits, real XLSX writing and unconditional browser cleanup. No permission/budget/contract changes. Remove the model-added consent branch and its supporting tasks: they are unrequested business actions. Remove the contradictory record_missing_url_product task: requires is mandatory, so an unconditional missing-URL assertion after a nonnull-URL assertion would always fail. Do not infer an error from interface text.

The r2 proposal also forwards entire snapshots, mixes extraction with top-ten selection and uses LLM interpretation for product/row/status copying. Correct these through existing typed bindings. A bounded query-to-search-URL conversion is allowed to replace the home-page/control/submit route; it must encode only query and add no filter. Otherwise retain the actual search route without unrequested interactions. No extra discovery is needed.

1. Retain complete producer evidence. Before using either search or product pages, attach ordered local requires using real output values: success==true, observationSnapshot!=null, captureTruncated==false and manifestTruncated==false. Use the declared snapshot fields, not a made-up complete flag. Preserve short-circuit null guards. Keep full snapshots separately; extraction inputs contain only their bounded pages, not content or the whole envelope.

2. Typed original records: one minimal foreach per acquisition over field(output(acquisition, observationSnapshot), pages), with body.tasks empty and body.outputs [pageRecords = field(item, records)]. Flatten its exported record arrays exactly once when originals are needed. Never use learned mapping to copy records. field selects one declared object property and takes its object in items; never field on an array or a dotted field name.

3. Each extraction binds input named pages to the original complete page array and explicitly declares each:{input:pages,output:candidates}. resultType is an object with required candidates:array<array<Candidate>>, because every original page produces one compact Candidate[]. Emit only reference and observedText copied verbatim (product facts may also include the observed tag if needed). Reference is the original opaque record.reference, unchanged. Keep URLs/actions on original records. No ranking, ten-product truncation, arbitrary URL pattern or guessed locator ancestry belongs in mapping. All original pages execute; empty arrays are valid page results, never invented placeholders. Do not add unobserved classifications or rank fields.

4. Search interpretation receives only flatten(extract_search_results.candidates) and query. It chooses the first at most ten product-title identities in their observed order, not URLs or rewritten facts. Output selectedIds is string[] with an explicit maxItems:10; choose only offered nonblank unchanged references, preserve repeated selections, and add no sponsored filter/deduplication. Use an explicit nonempty result contract where required for successful work; a genuinely unusable acquisition/selection must fail truthfully instead of making an empty identity or fake error row. Before the effectful visit loop, local requires must evaluate lookup(offeredCandidates,selectedIds) != null, then its items resolve lookup(flatten(originalPageRecords),selectedIds), using literal port:reference. Each visit navigates to the exact original item's href with an explicit nonnull guard. Lookup operands are [records,IDs], not reversed.

5. Product interpretation receives only flattened compact fact candidates and returns three nullable original IDs for name, description, price. It selects one complete relevant offered description block by unchanged ID. A feature/characteristics/descriptive-text block is eligible without a Description heading. Several suitable blocks are not absence: choose one. Null is permitted only for genuine absence or uncertain association with the current subject. Never use interface controls as descriptions. No joining, synthesis, trimming, paraphrase or rewriting. For each nonnull ID, first strictly lookup against offered candidates, then against original page records. Project text inside a typed item scope. The null alternative produces permitted null; never substitute an unrelated URL or interface control label as a fact/error. Lookup returns an array, even for one ID: do not field/index that array. The existing tested pattern is a conditional on ID!=null: body foreach(maxItems:1,items:lookup(originals,[ID]),requires:lookup(offered,[ID])!=null) exports text=field(item,text), and the condition scope exports values=that text array; otherwise exports values=[null]. Both alternatives have the same nullable-string-array port. Necessary nested bounded foreach scopes over these singleton values can bind name/description/price scalars and export a nonnull product object; use captures/ancestor bindings correctly. Pure typed scopes compile deterministically, never learned reconnection. error comes only from producer error_message, not an interpreted explanation. Keep the exact original navigation target for the action and independent oracle. Preserve accepted public fields name, description, price, error, all nullable inside a nonnull record. Keep navigation URL separate; do not add public fields. Field/port names must consistently follow this accepted interface.

6. Export product records directly from the visit scope. Flatten only real arrays of arrays; retain an existing typed bounded projection if needed to prove the accepted rows maxItems:10 and assemble four cells from each product. No interpret or extract may copy typed product records, reconnect IDs, assemble rows, or decide a status from already-typed booleans. Use a header literal [nom,description,prix,erreur] and bind writer.rows via flatten([[headerRow],productRows]); nesting means array(items:[array(items:[headerRow]),productRows]) is the single operand to flatten. This must produce one header plus up to ten product rows. Do not drop the header because it makes eleven total workbook rows; only product records are bounded by ten. Keep exact strings and null positions.

7. Require successful writing before claiming success, and require the writer's declared filePath to be nonnull before exporting it to the accepted nonnullable filePath output. Use typed value/outputs for that final assertion and status; root filePath comes from document_write.filePath, success from the validated real writer result, products from the checked deterministic products, browserClosed from close_browser.closed. Keep all these validations before finally cleanup. Preserve every accepted output's requiredness, nullability and cardinality. Do not omit root outputs or cleanup during restructuring.

Use only discovered contracts and current TaskPlan syntax. Keep pure plumbing in consumer bindings/scope outputs where possible, but retain minimal typed foreach projections/nullable scopes when existing bindings require them. Do not emit JavaScript, invent an operator, weaken contracts, change permissions or request another discovery. Preserve all actual observed values and the original requirements.
